factors.summary: The USD 500m sukuk was repaid ahead of its 8 April 2026 maturity, and Fitch upgraded the Maldives to CCC- from CC around June 2026. Moody's has held Caa2 with a stable outlook since 27 Nov 2025. Gross reserves fell from ~USD 1.3bn in March 2026 to USD 547m at end-September, and usable reserves fell to USD 169.8m after the final USD 50m repayment of the SBI T-bill facility (17 Sep) and FX sales to banks. India extended its INR 30bn (~USD 320m) RBI swap drawdown by three months in October 2026. Fitch counts this drawdown in gross but not usable reserves and puts external debt service at ~USD 535m in H2 2026, lower in 2027. The World Bank (June 2026) puts PPG debt at ~130% of GDP in 2025, heading above 140%, and the 2027 budget plans MVR 2.6bn of new bonds/sukuk plus a MVR 2.3bn Sovereign Development Fund drawdown. There is no IMF programme; the 2026 Article IV mission ran 4-14 June 2026.

factors.summary: The Maldives imports nearly all its energy, mainly diesel from Oman, and most of it is used for power generation, which also drives desalination. After Hormuz shipping halted in late Feb/early Mar 2026, STO raised retail diesel 26% to MVR 17.54/L and petrol 19% to MVR 16.01/L on 5 March, and wholesale diesel in Malé rose 65% to MVR 27.22/L. LPG fills were halved temporarily in mid-March. Officials described stocks as close to one month of cover, the maximum storage allows. Retail prices have been held since March using subsidies and STO profits while Brent traded between USD 97 and 112 in October 2026; tanker attacks in Hormuz continued on 30 Oct. The World Bank recommends phasing out blanket subsidies, which points to the price hike as the more likely route to resolution than a physical shortage.

factors.summary: Greater Malé depends entirely on diesel-powered MWSC desalination. A fire at the plant on 4 Dec 2014 left about 130,000 people without piped water, and India, China and Bangladesh shipped water in. In January 2026 MWSC began building two 13,000 t tanks intended to double Malé's storage. Outer islands rely on rainwater and groundwater; NDMA ships emergency desalinated water to up to 80 islands each December-April dry season, according to HRW (May 2025). During the 2016 El Niño, 45 islands ran short in the hottest dry season in 18 years. In March 2026 Malé's mayor warned that fuel stocks for water production were thin, but no supply failure occurred.

factors.summary: NOAA CPC (8 Oct 2026) reports a Niño-3.4 anomaly of +2.1°C, a better than 83% chance of a strong-to-very-strong El Niño, and a 70-83% chance of a historic event through Nov-Jan, persisting into Jan-Mar 2027. In April 2026 NOAA put the Maldives on bleaching 'Watch' and expected escalation to Alert Level 1. In 1998 hard-coral cover fell from 44.9% to 7.3%, and further heavy losses followed in 2016 and 2024. Reefs underpin dive tourism and live-bait tuna fishing; catches hit historic lows in 2024 and are again poor in 2026. Swell surges flooded parts of Malé on 26 Jul 2026, and continuous rain flooded the whole city on 21 Oct 2026.

factors.summary: On 4 Apr 2026 voters rejected the government's constitutional amendment 68.7% to 31.3%, and the opposition MDP narrowly out-won the PNC in local councils (247 to 246 seats) and kept all five city councils. Daily opposition protests from April led to about 20 arrests, police use of pepper spray and Tasers, and the jailing of two journalists after the Adhadhu documentary. Former presidents Yameen, Nasheed and Solih formed a press-freedom coalition on 15 May 2026, and RSF dropped the Maldives four places. The PNC still holds 74 of 93 Majlis seats. New friction centres on the Eagle Hills Rasmalé deal signed in Dubai on 21 Sep 2026, which nationalist and religious groups (Jamiyyathul Salaf) oppose; a rally is planned for 6 Nov 2026. Fiscal austerity in the 2027 budget (cabinet cut to 15 ministries, 33% SOE job cuts announced) adds grievances. India-China competition is now managed: India rolled over its support, China deferred debt and supplies most grants.

factors.summary: Between 200 and ~300 Maldivians are reported to have joined groups in Iraq and Syria, among the highest per-capita rates worldwide, and police said at least 423 attempted to travel. Past attacks include the Sultan Park bomb (Sep 2007, 12 foreigners injured), the ISIS-claimed Mahibadhoo boat arson (Apr 2020) and the IED that injured former President Nasheed (May 2021). In March 2025 three people were arrested for plotting attacks in Malé and nearby islands in support of Islamic State; they were charged in October 2025. The US advisory remains 'exercise increased caution' due to terrorism. In October 2026 former defence minister Moosa Ali Jaleel was appointed head of the National Counter Terrorism Centre. Anti-Israel sentiment linked to the Iran war and the Rasmalé dispute is an aggravating but unquantified factor.

factors.summary: Dengue has been above baseline since about October 2025: 424 cases in December 2025, 647 in January 2026 and 591 in March 2026, roughly 8.6 times March 2025. By 15 April 2026 there had been 1,908 cases and 3 deaths, 82% of them in the atolls (WHO SEARO bulletin). A 17-year-old died in Muli in April 2026. HPA also reported 7,792 diarrhoeal cases in January 2026. El Niño warmth and water storage in containers during dry spells favour Aedes breeding. Chronic import stress has already caused months-long shortages of some medicines, such as thalassaemia chelation drugs, in 2026.

countries.headline: Usable FX reserves of about USD 170m and a short Indian swap rollover make a balance-of-payments crisis the main risk, compounded by high fuel prices and a record El Niño.
countries.method: P(national crisis) is calculated like the global model: correlation factor × [1 − (1 − base rate) × Π(1 − P_factor × share_national_crisis)]. Both national factors and relevant global factors are included. "National crisis" means an event requiring national crisis management in the Maldives and affecting large parts of the population for several days.

countries.summary: Balance-of-payments stress is the dominant risk. After repaying its USD 500m sukuk in April 2026, the government has seen gross reserves fall from about USD 1.3bn in March to USD 547m at end-September, with usable reserves at USD 170m and falling USD 20–30m a month; India rolled over a USD 320m swap only to around late January 2027, and China's 2025 debt-relief terms remain undisclosed. The Hormuz closure raised retail diesel 26% in March and cut tourist arrivals by a fifth in March–April; arrivals have since nearly recovered, but the World Bank expects only 0.7% growth in 2026 and public debt is about 125–130% of GDP. Growth forecasts diverge widely (World Bank 0.7%, ADB 1.0%, IMF 3.0%, Ministry of Finance 5.3%), and no IMF programme is in place. Politics are tense after the ruling PNC lost the April referendum and local elections, but it holds 74 of 93 Majlis seats; the Rasmalé land deal is the new flashpoint. A record El Niño raises the risk of mass coral bleaching, dry-season water shortages on outer islands and dengue into the March–May 2027 hot season.

factors.summary: The 17 Oct 2026 national day drew 550,000 (Interior Ministry) and the following weekend saw looting and arson, with at least 3,000 shops damaged and 145 in custody in Paris alone on 19 Oct; Lecornu ordered localised curfews and said a state of emergency was possible 'if useful'. Turnout then fell to 410,000 on 24 Oct (1,314 arrests, 53 officers injured) and 320,000 on 31 Oct (290 arrests), with 70,000 police and gendarmes deployed. Students demand 250,000 more university places, the end of Parcoursup and 200 EUR/month more in grants; Macron has promised an admissions overhaul. Parliamentary risk is separate but linked: the PS calls its stance on the 2027 budget a 'sommation' and threatens censure if the text does not move, LFI will file censure if 49.3 is used, and the RN says Marine Le Pen will decide. Lecornu has survived every censure motion since October 2025, mostly thanks to PS abstention, and Macron has said he would dissolve the Assemblee if Lecornu were censured, which deters some deputies.

Moody's kept Aa3 with a negative outlook on 23 Oct, while S&P (A+) reviews on 27 Nov and Fitch held A+ on 28 Aug. The deficit is expected at 5.4% of GDP in 2026 after 5.1% in 2025; the 2027 bill targets 5% with about 43 bn EUR of new savings, but OFCE forecasts 5.4% in 2027 and growth of only 0.4-0.5%. Public debt is about 119% of GDP. ECB President Lagarde said the solution 'lies at home in France' and Banque de France governor Emmanuel Moulin said conditions for ECB intervention were not met, so a TPI backstop is not assured.

factors.summary: Vigipirate has been at its highest level, 'urgence attentat', with Interior Minister Laurent Nunez calling for maximum vigilance in May 2026. On 28 Mar 2026 police foiled an incendiary-device attack on Bank of America in Paris; Nunez linked it to the Middle East war and to the pro-Iranian label HAYI, whose attacks in France, Belgium and the Netherlands have used minors recruited online for 500-1,000 EUR. In July 2026 the DGSI disrupted a suspected Islamist plot against a Sarcelles synagogue (weapons car found 11 Jul). On 23 Oct 2026 a gunman shooting from a car in Trappes and La Verriere killed one man and wounded five; the PNAT took the case and Macron called it a 'racist terrorist attack', with the suspect reportedly seeking revenge for the 17 Oct looting. Threat streams therefore include jihadist, Iran-proxy and far-right actors, in a climate of street unrest and an election campaign.

On 13 Jul 2026 Paris attributed a long-running cyber-espionage campaign to the FSB (Turla) and moved to summon the Russian ambassador and sanction nine people and four entities. Days before the October protests, Nunez presented a plan to harden energy, transport and telecom sites against Russian hybrid attacks, and French intelligence has warned of hybrid attacks around 2027 elections. No destructive attack in France has yet been formally attributed to a state; the July 2024 rail and telecom sabotage was linked by investigators to the far left.

factors.summary: The Iran war remains in an armed pause with Hormuz effectively closed to vessels that do not coordinate with Iran. Iranian negotiators left Doha on 1 November after three days of Qatari mediation; an official says a draft proposal for a US deal is circulating and a follow-up meeting is possible, but foreign ministry spokesman Baghaei says the strait will not reopen until the US blockade ends and Iran's conditions are met, and says 'the ball is in the US court'. According to Axios, Trump prefers to give diplomacy more time after Netanyahu pressed him on 1 November to resume strikes right after the midterms; the military option remains open and Trump says one or two sites, including Pickaxe Mountain, still need to be dealt with. Attacks on shipping continue: a Qatari LNG carrier was hit in Gulf waters on 30 October, and UKMTO reported a tanker struck by two projectiles 72 nm east of Ras Al Khafji late on 1 November, far up the Gulf. The IRGC claims two tankers hit mines; this is unverified. CENTCOM says the blockade has redirected 144 vessels, while US Treasury Secretary Bessent's claim that non-Iranian transits are back to pre-war levels conflicts with UKMTO incident data and should be treated with caution. The Saudi–Houthi war continues, with a Houthi missile intercepted over southern Saudi Arabia on 2 November, and Israel's election left no majority bloc. On 2 November oil fell 7.6% to about $104.8 on reports that Iran's leadership authorised talks; whether this is a real shift or a pause before the post-election period is disputed.

factors.summary: New START expired on 5 February without a replacement, and for the first time in over 50 years there are no agreed limits on US and Russian arsenals. The IAEA says it has been blind to Iran's programme since June 2025, cannot verify the roughly 440 kg of 60%-enriched uranium, and has seen construction activity at Pickaxe Mountain; the Board referred Iran to the Security Council in September. Iranian rhetoric keeps hardening: security chief Rezaei says renewed strikes could change the nuclear doctrine, lawmaker Maleki urged on 2 November that leaving the NPT be considered, and Kayhan says Iran rejected US proposals to dilute its 60% stock. Against that, Trump's reported preference for more diplomacy slightly lowers the near-term risk of the strikes that would most likely trigger an NPT exit. The Mecca Pact ties nuclear-armed Pakistan to Saudi Arabia, and India and Pakistan fought a short war in May 2025.

factors.summary: A record El Niño is under way. IRI (19 Oct) reports a September Niño 3.4 anomaly of +2.84 °C and a weekly value of +3.3 °C centred on 14 October, with El Niño at 100% probability through spring 2027; the following week reached about +3.4 °C. WMO expects a peak around December with an Oct–Dec anomaly of about +3.7 °C, and Carbon Brief notes the event has grown faster than any on record and that seasonal models have never been tested on an event this large. Most of the global temperature and rainfall impact typically lags by several months, so the main food-system effects fall in 2027. At the same time the Hormuz crisis is causing fertiliser shortages; about a third of global fertiliser trade passed through the strait before the war.

globalSummary: Over the next 30 days the picture is still dominated by the Gulf: Hormuz is effectively closed, a record El Niño is building and Ukraine's grid is under heavy attack before winter. On 2 November Brent settled near $104.8 (down 7.6%) after reports that Iran's supreme leader had given the government authority to hold talks and Iran's president said Tehran wants to resolve the dispute through dialogue; Trump had earlier said he would not strike before the 3 November midterms. Markets have sold off on settlement hopes earlier in this war and then reversed when fighting resumed, and Tehran still conditions any reopening of the strait on an end to the US blockade, so analysts disagree on whether this is the start of a bargaining phase or a pause while the US military option stays open. Monetary conditions are tightening: the Fed held on 28 October with two dissents for a hike and a December hike is priced, which raises the risk of a financial shock on top of high energy costs. France's 10-year yield passed 5% in October with the spread to Bunds near 160 bp, and Italy is added to the country panels this week. The next tests are the US vote (3 Nov), the French general strike (5 Nov), Norges Bank (5 Nov), the US jobs report (6 Nov) and APEC (18–19 Nov).

method.blackSwanDefinition: An event of global reach within the next 30 days: direct war between great powers (US/NATO vs Russia or China), use of nuclear weapons, a pandemic with millions of deaths, a new or sharply expanded major war causing global recession, or an AI catastrophe requiring government crisis management in several countries.
method.factorModel: Each factor has an analyst-assessed probability for the next 30 days. Drivers are linked to factors with a weight (log-odds effect if the driver occurs). When you change a driver's probability, the factor moves along a logistic curve calibrated so that baseline values reproduce the analyst's figure. One driver can affect several factors.
method.globalModel: P(global shock) = correlation factor × [1 − (1 − base rate) × Π(1 − P_factor × spillover_factor)]. Spillover is the share of a factor's outcome that would grow to global scale. The correlation factor (0.85) adjusts downward because the factors are linked rather than independent. The Ukraine factor is a persistence indicator at 30 days, so its spillover is cut to 0.5%.

norway.headline: According to the government, Norway faces its most serious security situation since the Second World War. For most people this winter, though, the most concrete risk is electricity prices in southern Norway, not war.
norway.method: P(national crisis) is calculated like the global model: correlation factor × [1 − (1 − base rate) × Π(1 − P_factor × share_national_crisis)]. Both Norwegian and global factors (pandemic, Taiwan, hybrid war, economy) are included. "National crisis" means an event requiring national crisis management and affecting large parts of the population for several days.

Reservoirs in southern Norway are the lowest in 20 years, and October prices in the south are around NOK 1.3–1.5/kWh. The economy is robust: NAV unemployment is 2.1% and the policy rate 4.5%. Norway has fuel stocks for only 20 days, and the government proposes doubling them in the 2027 budget.
